summary: The automated timing-data script found 0 experiment commits since milestone 2026.05.245 activation, producing a twenty-first consecutive empty-timing-window retro. No wall-clock minutes or experiment IDs are available from the authoritative TIMING DATA block; all interpretive sections reflect that absence honestly. Both RTX 3090 GPUs were idle (0% utilization, 5 MB allocated each) at retro time with no compute-bound tasks in the timing window to flag.
bottlenecks_identified: Timing-capture gap: the automated timing script again found 0 experiment commits at retro time — this is the twenty-first consecutive empty window, indicating a structural misalignment between when experiments commit to the authoritative git log and when the retro script scans.
No compute-bound experiments were logged; therefore GPU idle status cannot be assessed and DualGPURunner relevance is indeterminate this milestone.
improvements_suggested: Widen the timing-script look-back window to capture same-session experiment commits that land after milestone activation but before the retro task fires.
Trigger the retro task with a minimum 60-second delay after the capstone artifact commits, or have the capstone explicitly flush the git index before the retro fires.

Add a fallback path in the timing script: if 0 commits are found for the active milestone, scan ops/changelog.md for lines matching the milestone prefix and surface them as unverified timing hints (clearly labeled) so the retro is not entirely dark.
Both GPUs were idle at retro time; for the next milestone, activate the first compute-bound experiment in the same session as planning so GPU cycles are captured while the retro window is still open.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the timing-data capture script to include within-session experiment commits: this is the root cause of 21 consecutive empty-window retros and eliminates the blind spot in every future operational analysis.
Activate the next milestone's first experiment in the same session as planning, ensuring at least one commit lands within the timing window before the retro fires.

Add an ops/changelog.md fallback to the retro script so that even when git-log returns 0 commits, the retro can surface milestone-tagged changelog entries as advisory (not authoritative) context — giving future operators a non-empty retro to act on.
meta_reflection: Twenty-one consecutive empty-timing-window retros point to a structural process gap, not an isolated event. The retro script and the experiment-commit pipeline are misaligned by design: experiments run, commit, and are logged in ops/changelog.md well before the retro fires, but the git-log query used by the timing script does not see them. Until the timing script is fixed, every operational retro will report 0 experiments and offer no bottleneck signal — making the retro artifact structurally uninformative. The single most valuable process change this milestone can motivate is landing the timing-script fix before 2026.05.246 activates.
